title: SKP Business / Pipeline
description: Business / pipeline counters across the three services that emit domain meters (orchestrator / keeper / processor), plus the WebApi represented by ASP.NET Core request metrics only (it registers no domain meter - BPD-03). The two template variables are populated from the process_runtime_dotnet_* family emitted by OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Runtime 1.15.0 on net8.0 (research F-1) - the one instrumentation every service class shares. A future net9.0 upgrade would rename that family to dotnet_* and blank both dropdowns; scripts/phase-87-dashboard-lint.ps1 rule S8 hard-fails on any dotnet_* reference so that regression surfaces hermetically in ~5s instead of as a silently empty dashboard.

panels.title: Orchestrator consumed vs sent (conservation)
panels.description: Overlaying consumed and sent on one axis is what makes the conservation relationship readable at a glance (BPD-02). Both targets are Class A (VER-01): they have live series on a healthy stack and must never carry an or vector(0) guard - lint rule C7 enforces that, because a guarded Class A signal renders 0 and lets a fully stalled pipeline pass the live proof.

panels.title: Keeper consumed vs sent (conservation)
panels.description: GUARDED ON PURPOSE - both targets carry 'or vector(0)', and that is not decoration. keeper_messages_consumed / keeper_messages_sent increment ONLY inside RecoveryConsumerBase.Consume / CountSent, so they fire only during a recovery event: research F-4 measured zero live series and Pitfall 6 records that both names are absent from the entire 15-day Prometheus __name__ index. That places them in REQUIREMENTS.md VER-01 Class B ('any counter with no live series on a healthy stack'), so this is a properly guarded Class-B panel, not a Class-A panel with a hole in it. Lint rule C3 requires the guard on EVERY expression referencing these two counters anywhere in this file, and plan 87-05 STEP F classifies an expression Class A or Class B purely by the presence of this substring - its traffic drive (STEP E) is a happy-path FanOutSeeder run with no fault scenario, so an unguarded target here would be asserted as Class A and would fail the live proof. HOW TO READ A FLAT 0: 'no recovery traffic in this window'. It does NOT mean 'keeper down' - the keeper liveness signal is the Class-A 'Keeper L2 probe heartbeat' panel.

panels.title: Processor consumed vs sent by image (conservation)
panels.description: The VAR-04 correction in force (research F-6). Every source="processor" series carries the unresolved_0.0.0 MLBL-03 sentinel on service_name, so service_name CANNOT discriminate processor images; identityName (carrying {db.Name}_{db.Version}) is the discriminator, and it exists only on these two business counters. No processor panel on this dashboard groups by service_name - lint rule C5 enforces the identityName grouping. Both targets are Class A (VER-01): they have live series on a healthy stack and must never carry an 'or vector(0)' guard, which lint rule C7 enforces.

panels.title: Cross-tier conservation gap (orchestrator sent - processor consumed)
panels.description: This is the axis the 7-scenario resilience sweep scores on (MG-1 conservation), evaluated over the dashboard window rather than over a sweep run. A sustained positive value means the orchestrator dispatched work the processors never consumed. Class A (VER-01): both counters have live series on a healthy stack, so this expression carries NO 'or vector(0)' guard - lint rule C7 enforces that, because a guarded Class-A expression renders 0 and would let a fully stalled pipeline pass the live proof. Threshold: green base, red at 1 - the operand is an integer message count, so 'red above 0' is 'red at 1'.

panels.title: Per-processor dispatch gap
panels.description: The analyzer's historical bottleneck view expressed in the current counter names: dispatched-minus-consumed per processor identity. processorId is the DB identity GUID carried on both business counters - note it is a LABEL, not a metric, and it does not match the lint's processor_\w+ family regex because that regex requires the underscore (pinned by the lint's -SelfTest fixture (e)). Class A (VER-01): unguarded by design, enforced by lint rule C7.
